newsitem.title: GERMANY: One-point VAT hike enough for tax reform - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: One-point VAT hike enough for tax reform - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that an increase of one percentage point in value-added tax would be enough to help finance a major tax reform planned to take effect in 1999.
"Based on the concept that I am following we will manage with an increase of one point," Waigel told reporters in Munich after a meeting of his Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) party.
Waigel came under heavy attack over the weekend from regional leaders of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), sister party of his CSU, about the plans to hike VAT by two points.
Waigel received the full backing from Kohl over the weekend, but criticism of his handling of the tax reforms by up-and-coming CDU politicians continued on Monday.

Under Waigel's tax reform plans, to be finalised on Thursday, income taxes should be cut drastically, with the top rate falling below 40 percent from 53 percent and the entry rate to under 20 percent from 26 percent now.
The cuts in direct taxes will be financed by scrapping tax breaks and the one-point increase in VAT.
